text: Fill in each blank with the correct term or value from the section you just read.
questions: In cystic fibrosis the F508del mutation causes the CFTR protein to misfold, and ER quality control targets it for destruction by the *proteasome:Which cytoplasmic machine degrades misfolded proteins sent back from the ER?*.
A sweat chloride concentration of *60:Recall the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation consensus cut-off for the sweat test.* mmol/L or more supports the diagnosis of cystic fibrosis.

In hereditary spherocytosis a weakened *spectrin-ankyrin/spectrin:Which cytoskeletal proteins form the meshwork on the inner face of the red-cell membrane?* skeleton allows the red cell to lose membrane and become a sphere.

In paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria a PIGA mutation blocks synthesis of the *GPI/glycosylphosphatidylinositol:Which type of lipid anchor holds certain proteins on the outer leaflet of the membrane?* anchor, so complement-regulatory proteins CD55 and CD59 are lost from the red-cell surface.

Corrector drugs help the misfolded CFTR protein fold correctly, while the potentiator *ivacaftor:One class of drug fixes folding (corrector); the other fixes gating (potentiator).* helps the channel open once it reaches the membrane.

overallFeedback.feedback: Each disease illustrates a different membrane or organelle failure: in F508del CF, misfolded CFTR is targeted for proteasomal degradation, and a sweat chloride of 60 mmol/L or more supports the diagnosis in the appropriate clinical context (a positive result requires confirmation on a separate date or by an independent diagnostic method, not a single reading alone); the spectrin-ankyrin skeleton fails in spherocytosis; the GPI anchor is missing in PNH; and corrector plus potentiator drugs (e.g. ivacaftor) rescue CFTR by fixing folding and gating respectively.
